detail.longDescription: RE: https:// piaille.fr/@benjamin/117171947 304939705 As part of my anti-fascism, I changed my domain from davidculley.com to davidculley.eu a while ago. I thought it merely a symbolic gesture, but maybe it's not so symbolic after all. The top-level domain .com is controlled by Verisign, a greedy US company. Depending on US companies is problematic as can be seen by what happened to the Italian anti-fascism collective. Verisign also lobbied hard so that they're allowed to increase their prices by 7% every year in 4 out of 6 years. A few years ago it had cost only $9 to renew your .com domain. Soon it'll already be at $15 a year. Maybe 7% doesn't sound much per individual domain, but consider there are millions if not billions of domains that need to be renewed every year. This is a cashcow for Verisign. They make their profits through quantity. They provide nothing at all in return for their price increases. Verisign is a leech. Meanwhile a .eu domain costs $5 a year. There's no monopoly on the .eu top-level domain. The EU Commission chooses from a pool of applicants every few years and the current mandate is given to a Belgian company. I'm not a commercial entity. I don't sell you anything. I'm a person within the EU with a personal homepage. I'm aware the EU has its problems too (Europ€an value$), especially at its borders, but for now the .eu TLD represents me better than the .com TLD. Cutting your dependencies on US companies is not merely symbolic as can be seen by what happened this week to anti-fascists worldwide. # fascism # capitalism # WebDev
